correctness.rationale: Exact state reduction uses T_k=|A_k cap B_k|; its three transitions sum to k²-t. The first falling-factorial moment gives a telescoping upper probability bound; the second provides E[(T_k)_2] ≤ k²(k²−1)/(n(n+1)). Summing the resulting harmonic defect proves all n≥2 inequalities and asymptotic constant. Independent edge-state rational recursions and full six-edge arrival enumeration corroborate finite cases, but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A crown graph is a canonical minimal symmetric defect of a complete bipartite substrate: it retains perfect matchings yet greedy irreversible dimers occasionally jam. The theorem isolates the rare physical jamming probability with sharp universal prefactor 2 and quantified logarithmic finite-size convergence, revealing information lost in the near-unit limiting coverage fraction. The second-moment control is structural, not a tabulated small-case census.
